rows.name: SortableJS
rows.reason: SortableJS provides cross-list dragging, grouping, and stable-ID serialization for moving components between saved groups. Persistence, account authorization, business rules, and large-list rendering remain application responsibilities.

rows.name: Laravel with Livewire and small JavaScript components
rows.reason: Laravel/Livewire supports a PHP-centered rebuild; drag/drop needs JavaScript. Laravel 9 requires PHP 8+, not a contradiction with unspecified runtime. Legacy/Perl compatibility, effort, grouping/performance and prepaid/Excel behavior remain unverified.

rows.name: DirectX
rows.reason: Windows graphics and multimedia APIs do not supply the browser UI, user accounts, database application backend or exports required for this website.

rows.name: Symfony with Symfony UX
rows.reason: PHP/Stimulus UX supports interactive pages/charts; legacy compatibility and workflow completeness unproven. Custom drag/drop persistence and spreadsheet/payment integration required. Current Symfony 6.2 maintenance notices cannot establish January 2023 status.

rows.name: Inertia.js with Vue and Laravel
rows.reason: Vue editor connects to Laravel routing/controllers through Inertia. Requires modern JavaScript components/build workflow. Inertia page unreadable; verification relies on Laravel primary documentation.

rows.name: Directus
rows.reason: Directus offers database APIs, authentication and access control as a possible backend. Grouping UI and business-rule preservation need planning; no mandatory violation or necessary rule-discarding was established.

rows.name: Django
rows.reason: Its ORM, routing and administrative interface support the database-backed site, although preserving PHP/Perl business logic requires translation or a separate service.

rows.name: Laravel 9 with Breeze
rows.reason: PHP application foundation with Breeze authentication fits account/database workflows. Requires modern PHP and explicit legacy PHP/Perl adaptation; the starter-kit page itself is undated.

rows.name: DirectX
rows.reason: Native Win32/UWP graphics/gaming APIs mismatch an interactive web framework; list/group/account transfer unestablished. Exclusion asserts neither a PHP-only requirement nor explicit lack of business-logic preservation support.

rows.name: Laravel Excel 3.1
rows.reason: Laravel Excel can turn the requesting user's selected components and groups into a downloadable Excel workbook. Export queries require user scoping, explicit columns, and memory assessment for large datasets.

rows.name: Laravel with Inertia.js and Vue
rows.reason: Laravel controllers with Vue pages support substantial client-side state. Requires Vue/components, asset tooling and legacy PHP/Perl integration. Comparative delivery time and thousand-item interaction performance were not benchmarked.

rows.name: Livewire 2
rows.reason: PHP/Blade components enable interactive selection/forms/grouping without full reloads. Keep drag motion client-side and prototype complex state; versioned live documentation has no verified publication date.

rows.name: Chart.js
rows.reason: Chart.js can render graphs of backend-computed component usage counts. Does not calculate business usage metrics; inspected evidence is later than the question cutoff, and version 3.9.1 retrieval failed.

rows.name: Django
rows.reason: Django is a possible Python web alternative with PHP/Perl migration work unresolved. Preserving business logic does not require identical language; preservation impossibility, deadline and domain-integration claims remain unestablished.

rows.name: Vue 3 over the existing PHP/Perl backend
rows.reason: Vue 3 incrementally replaces frontend interaction over PHP/Perl, reducing initial migration scope. It remains partial: endpoints, authorization, drag/drop synchronization, list performance and reusable backend operations require application work.

rows.name: Laravel Cashier for Stripe
rows.reason: Stripe billing/payment integration may support prepaid purchases if Stripe fits. Credits and entitlement accounting still need application logic; subscription billing is not automatically the correct prepaid model.

rows.name: Directus
rows.reason: Provides database APIs, authentication and access control for saved components and groups; custom drag-and-drop, payment integration and legacy business logic still require work.

rows.name: Django 4.1
rows.reason: Django 4.1 supplies models, routing and administration for component/group management. Existing PHP/Perl logic needs translation or exposure, and the custom customer editor still requires development.
